subject: Nexus Health — Private VPC deployment, audit scope & pricing
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@nexushealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, procurement@nexushc.com
Date: 2026-10-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Nexus Health — Private VPC deployment, audit scope & pricing

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week. Nexus Health is ready to move forward with a Private (VPC) deployment in us-east-1 but we need to align on a few non-standard items before we can sign: 

- Data residency: all customer PHI and logs must remain in the US (no cross-border replication).
- Audit rights: Nexus requests quarterly audit access (customer-appointed third-party auditor) with up to 3 onsite days or remote evidence review when applicable.
- SLA: target 99.95% availability for our dedicated environment with financial credits for breaches.
- Pricing: because of the integration work and long-term commitment (36 months), we are requesting a 20% discount off list for the first 24 months and a 3-year prepayment option.

Attached: Nexus_RFP_20261010.pdf and our Security Questionnaire (Nexus_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx). Please advise next steps and whether Redwood can accommodate the audit window and discount request.

Best,
Maria Santos
Head of Platform Partnerships
Nexus Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@nexushealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexus Health — Private VPC deployment, audit scope & pricing

Maria — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. We're excited to partner. High level next steps: 

1) Security (cc'd Aditya) will review the questionnaire and propose a practical audit approach that balances Nexus' needs and our standard controls.
2) I'll open a deal desk request for the discount and SLA exception and loop in Laura for pricing/contract cadence.
3) We should aim to get security and deal desk alignment before legal redlines.

Can you confirm whether Nexus requires onsite access every quarter for all evidence or if remote evidence review is acceptable for months without major scope changes? That will help Aditya scope the response.

I attached our initial intake note and will follow up internally today.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Santos <maria.santos@nexushealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Nexus Health — Private VPC deployment, audit scope & pricing

Hannah / Laura — reviewed Nexus' questionnaire and the request for quarterly onsite audits. Initial security position and suggested compromises below: 

- Data residency: OK for US-only hosting in us-east-1. We will guarantee no cross-region replication unless explicitly requested and approved by Redwood Security + customer PO.
- Audit rights: Quarterly onsite audits are operationally disruptive and present IP/exposure concerns. Proposed compromise: 
  * Primary: Remote evidence review against our SOC 2 controls and per-request export of redacted evidence (logs, configs) with 14 days' notice.
  * Escalation path: If Nexus' third-party auditor identifies scope gaps requiring onsite verification, we will allow a single onsite visit per 12-month period with a detailed NDA and escorted access.
- Logs & retention: We can commit to 13 months of customer access to audit logs (date/seq). Longer retention can be added as a paid option.
- Key management: We support customer-managed keys (Bring-Your-Own-KMS) subject to HSM availability in the deployment model; legal needs to confirm contract language.

I've attached a redline (Redwood_Nexus_Redline_v1.docx) with exact clause language and limits on data access and auditor scope. From a risk perspective the above keeps us compliant while addressing Nexus' assurance needs.

If Sales wants to pursue the 20% discount request, I need clarity on revenue/commitment (ACV and prepayment) to quantify risk.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: Nexus Health (NEX-2026-1423) — approval request for discount & audit carveouts

Vivek — quick ask for executive sign-off to move this deal forward. Summary below: 

- Account: Nexus Health (large regional health system)
- Requested: 20% discount first 24 months, 36-month commitment; quarterly audit with upto 3 onsite days; SLA 99.95%; option for 3-year prepayment.
- Our recommended commercial/contract position: 
  * Discount: approve up to 15% for first 24 months contingent on 3-year commitment and prepayment for year 1.
  * Audit: accept Aditya's proposed compromise (remote evidence review + 1 onsite/year escalation only).
  * SLA: 99.95% with standard credits; higher support tier purchased by Nexus.
- Economics: ACV at list $1.2M/year; at 15% discount first 24 months, effective first-year revenue reduction $180k — still within acceptable range given strategic value and references in healthcare.
- Conditions we require if you approve discount: 
  1) Prepayment for year 1 or a signed committed minimum spend schedule.
  2) Legal to include tight auditor scope/NDAs per Aditya's redline.
  3) Finance to approve billing milestone and recognize deferred revenue appropriately.

Can you confirm whether you approve the 15% discount and the audit compromise so I can finalize the commercial term sheet? We need executive ok by COB Monday to hit Nexus' procurement cycle.

Thanks — Hannah
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-17T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Nexus Health (NEX-2026-1423) — approval request for discount & audit carveouts

Hannah — thank you for the clear summary. I approve a capped commercial concession and the proposed audit compromise with the following mandatory conditions: 

1) Discount: authorize up to 12% off list for the first 24 months (not 15%). Any additional concession requires CFO sign-off.
2) Prepayment: require prepayment of year 1 or an irrevocable letter of credit covering the first 12 months.
3) Audit scope: accept Aditya's remote-first approach and allow one onsite visit per 12 months only if critical issues are raised; legal to use the redline verbatim with NDA and escort clauses.
4) SLA: agree to 99.95% but only with Nexus purchasing a Premium Support add-on and a defined MTTR for critical incidents in the SOW.
5) Finance: Laura to confirm the revenue treatment and ensure the margin impact is recorded; no additional internal concessions until Finance signs off.

Once Laura confirms finance/legal acceptance of the conditions, Sales can finalize the commercial term sheet and route to Nexus for signature.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales Operations & Strategy
Redwood Inference
